title: Healthcare and medicines
measures: Which healthcare content Google Ads restricts or prohibits (prescription drug services, restricted drug terms, speculative and experimental treatments, clinical trial recruitment, health insurance certification and others); states that ads and destinations are expected to follow local law and that ads exclusively for dental insurance coverage are not restricted.
limitations: Undated policy page that Google may change without notice; it does not list dental procedures such as implants as a restricted category, so implant ads are governed mainly by the general policies (misrepresentation, destination, personalized advertising).

title: Restricted targeting in Personalized advertising
measures: Lists Health among sensitive interest categories; advertisers promoting products or services in sensitive interest categories cannot use advertiser-curated audiences (customer match, your data segments, lookalike and custom segments) but may use predefined Google audiences.
limitations: Policy page; whether a given dental campaign is classed as a sensitive health category is decided by Google's review, not by the advertiser.

title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
measures: Quality Score is a 1–10 keyword-level diagnostic built from expected clickthrough rate, ad relevance and landing page experience (how relevant and useful the landing page is to people who click); it is not a key performance indicator and not an input in the ad auction.
limitations: Diagnostic only; components are relative to other advertisers on the same searches over the last 90 days.

title: Misrepresentation
measures: Prohibits failing to clearly disclose the payment model or full expense, pricing practices that create a misleading impression of cost, clickbait, using negative life events such as illness to pressure action, enticing users with an improbable result as the likely outcome, and promising offers that are unavailable or not easily found at the destination.
limitations: Policy page; enforcement examples are not exhaustive.

title: Destination requirements
measures: Landing pages must work on common browsers and devices, match the display URL domain, be crawlable by AdsBot, not be unnecessarily difficult to navigate and offer original content; phone numbers in call assets must be in service, relate to the advertised company and have voicemail.
limitations: Policy page; Google states it warns at least 7 days before suspension for these violations, which may change.

title: Measure calls from ads
measures: Call conversions can be counted by call duration above a minimum the advertiser sets, or by Google's AI analysing call recordings (limited to calls where both parties are in the U.S. or Canada); calls from website visits and calls via uploads (imported from another system) are separate conversion actions; recording can be disabled in account settings.
limitations: Feature availability and default settings change; the page does not address state recording-consent laws.

title: About call assets
measures: Call assets can be scheduled to show only when the business can accept calls; call reporting uses Google forwarding numbers; websites using dynamic number insertion cannot have phone numbers verified by source-code scanning and must verify domain ownership (Search Console link or Google tag in raw HTML) instead.
limitations: Product documentation; verification methods may change.

title: Add your phone number
measures: In addition to the primary business phone number, a Business Profile can list up to 2 more phone numbers (mobile or landline; not fax).
limitations: Does not state whether a call tracking number may be the primary number; that has to be read together with the representation guidelines.

title: Manage your local business links
measures: Profiles can carry booking and other action links (up to 10 per category, with a preferred link); third-party booking links can appear automatically and must be removed through the provider, which is required to process opt-outs within 5 business days.
limitations: Availability of booking links varies by category and region; not available through the Business Profile API.

title: Conversions vs. key events in Google Analytics
measures: Google Analytics calls important business actions key events; a conversion is the Google Ads-side action used to measure campaigns and optimise bidding, created from a key event.
limitations: Terminology page; says nothing about whether an event represents a new patient.

title: Regulation Z § 1026.24 Advertising
measures: For closed-end credit advertising, stating a triggering term (downpayment amount or percentage, number of payments or repayment period, payment amount, or finance charge) requires the ad to also state the downpayment, the repayment terms and the annual percentage rate.
limitations: Applies to credit advertisements as defined in Regulation Z; whether and how it applies to a practice promoting a third-party lender's plan is a question for counsel and the lender. Not legal advice.

title: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
measures: Defines INP as a measure of responsiveness to user interactions such as taps and key presses across a page visit; 200 milliseconds or less is good.
limitations: Last updated 2025-09-02 per the page. Field data is needed; lab tools approximate it.

title: Optimize Largest Contentful Paint
measures: Breaks LCP into sub-parts (server response, resource load delay and duration, render delay) and explains how to diagnose a slow largest element such as a hero image.
limitations: Last updated 2025-03-31 per the page. Technical guidance, not dental-specific.

title: Learn Forms: Autofill
measures: How browsers offer autofill and how autocomplete and other attributes help users avoid re-entering data such as names and addresses.
limitations: Developer guidance; browser behaviour varies.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum)
measures: Pointer targets should be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with spacing and other exceptions; the enhanced criterion 2.5.5 uses 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
limitations: Informative explanation of a standard, not a law.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.3.5: Identify Input Purpose
measures: Form fields collecting information about the user should expose their purpose programmatically (for example via autocomplete values) so browsers and assistive technology can help fill them.
limitations: Informative explanation of a standard, not a law.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.3.2: Labels or Instructions
measures: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input, so users know what information to enter.
limitations: Informative explanation of a standard, not a law.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.3.1: Error Identification
measures: When an input error is automatically detected, the item in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
limitations: Informative explanation of a standard, not a law.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.3.7: Redundant Entry
measures: Information a user has already entered in the same process should be auto-populated or available to select rather than requested again, with limited exceptions.
limitations: Informative explanation of a standard, not a law.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.2.6: Consistent Help
measures: Help mechanisms such as a contact phone number or contact link that repeat across pages should appear in the same relative order on each page.
limitations: Informative explanation of a standard, not a law.

title: Requirements
measures: Recommended hosting: PHP 8.3 or greater, MariaDB 10.11+ or MySQL 8.0+, HTTPS; older PHP and MySQL versions still work but have reached end of life and may expose sites to security vulnerabilities.
limitations: Recommendations change with each release cycle; retrieved values reflect the page on 2026-11-08.

title: Hardening WordPress
measures: Older versions of WordPress are not maintained with security updates; once a fix is released the information to exploit the vulnerability is likely public; automatic updates have existed since version 3.7; server software must also be kept secure.
limitations: General security guidance; plugin and theme risk depends on the specific extensions installed.

title: Plugin and themes auto-updates
measures: Since WordPress 5.5 administrators can opt in to automatic updates plugin by plugin and theme by theme, with email notifications after update attempts.
limitations: Auto-updates reduce patch lag but can introduce compatibility breaks; the page does not address testing.

title: REST API Handbook
measures: The WordPress REST API exposes posts, pages and other content as JSON so separate applications in any language can read and write site content; it underpins the block editor. This is the basis for using WordPress as a headless CMS.
limitations: Technical reference; does not compare hosting or maintenance cost.

title: Next.js Support Policy
measures: Major versions are in Active LTS until the next major, then Maintenance LTS (critical and security fixes only) for two years from initial release; on the retrieval date 16.x was Active LTS (released 21 Oct 2025) and 15.x Maintenance LTS with security releases extended through 31 Jan 2027.
limitations: Vendor policy; dates change with each major release.

title: How to create a static export of your Next.js application
measures: Next.js can export a site as static files for any static host; features that need a server, including cookies, rewrites, redirects, headers, incremental static regeneration, default image optimization and Server Actions, are unsupported in a static export.
limitations: Technical documentation for the current major version.

title: 18 U.S. Code § 2511 – Interception and disclosure of wire, oral, or electronic communications prohibited
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
measures: Section 2511(2)(d): it is not unlawful for a person not acting under color of law to intercept a communication where that person is a party or one of the parties has given prior consent, unless intercepted for a criminal or tortious purpose (the federal one-party consent baseline).
limitations: Unofficial reproduction of the U.S. Code; state laws can be stricter. Not legal advice.

title: Florida Statutes § 934.03 – Interception and disclosure of wire, oral, or electronic communications prohibited
measures: Section 934.03(2)(d): it is lawful for a person to intercept a wire, oral or electronic communication when all of the parties to the communication have given prior consent.
limitations: 2025 statute text; application depends on facts such as expectation of privacy. Not legal advice.

title: Reporter's Recording Guide: California
publisher: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press
measures: Summarises Cal. Penal Code § 632(a): all parties to a confidential communication, including by telephone, must consent to recording; § 632.7 requires all-party consent for calls involving a cellular or cordless phone regardless of confidentiality (Smith v. LoanMe, Cal. 2021); first offences punishable by fines up to $2,500.
limitations: Secondary legal summary written for journalists, last updated 2021-08 per the page; not the statute text and not legal advice. Check the current statute and ask counsel.

title: Reporter's Recording Guide: Texas
publisher: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press
measures: Summarises Tex. Penal Code § 16.02: a party to a telephone conversation, or a person with one party's consent, may lawfully record it unless for a criminal or tortious purpose (one-party consent).
limitations: Secondary legal summary written for journalists, last updated 2020-06 per the page; not the statute text and not legal advice. Check the current statute and ask counsel.

title: Reporter's Recording Guide: Georgia
publisher: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press
measures: Summarises Ga. Code §§ 16-11-62 and 16-11-66(a): a party to a communication, or a person with one party's prior consent, may record it (one-party consent).
limitations: Secondary legal summary written for journalists, last updated 2020-05 per the page; not the statute text and not legal advice. Check the current statute and ask counsel.
